resale_co.notes: The Borough's forms page lists the 'Certificate of Compliance Application Form (SALE OF PROPERTY, CCO)', and the application (updated September 15, 2026) has a 'Sale of Property' box, so a Borough certificate is part of a sale. The published fees are written for a two-family residence ($200.00, each additional unit $85.00 on the form), so it is not confirmed in writing whether a single-family sale needs this certificate or only the fire certificate; ask the office. Fees: Ordinance 2026-11 (adopted April 15, 2026) set CCO residential $200.00 and reinspection $85.00 (commercial $300.00). The Borough's 'FEE CHANGES 2025' web page still shows the older amounts ($175.00 two family, additional $50.00 per unit, reinspection $80.00), and the form labels the $85.00 as 'each additional unit' while the ordinance calls it reinspection. The ordinance amounts are used here. The form does not list what is inspected, lead time or validity. Office: 567 Boulevard, Kenilworth; Borough main number 908-276-9090 (on the form). Kenilworth also inspects non-owner-occupied rentals yearly through the Bureau of Fire Prevention (Ordinance 2026-08); that is a rental program, not a resale requirement.

requirements: Battery-only smoke and carbon monoxide alarms must be 10-year sealed battery units (since January 1, 2019), on each level and outside all bedroom areas
Hardwired (electric) smoke and CO alarms may not be replaced with battery alarms, and must be replaced after 10 years (date of manufacture is on the underside)
Electric CO alarms or combination smoke/CO alarms are required on each level and next to any fuel-burning appliance

Homes with a permanently installed generator, solar panels, battery storage or other secondary power source need a label (not handwritten) within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and the electric meter saying there are multiple power sources
The fire inspector contacts the applicant to review requirements before the inspection

fire_cert.notes: The Borough's fire application (scanned, dated November 2025) lists $100.00 / $160.00 for a 1 week turnaround and $150.00 / $210.00 when requested on less than 1 week, each with 1 re-inspection; inspections needing more than 1 re-inspection pay a second fee (the same fee again). Ordinance 2026-08 (adopted April 15, 2026) sets the sale fee at the annual-inspection amount ($100.00 single family, $160.00 two family) when requested two or more weeks in advance and gives one free re-inspection; it does not list a rush fee for sales (only a $50.00 expedited fee for landlords). The fire official's name and email come only from the state fire directory (survey 1/27/2026); the Borough site lists only the Fire Prevention Office number 908-276-8935. The form does not list a portable fire extinguisher.

other_items.detail: The Building Department follows up on all open permits with Notices of Violations and, in some cases, penalties; schedule final inspections to close them.

open_questions: Does a single-family sale need the Borough Certificate of Compliance / Continued Occupancy, or only a two-family or larger sale? The fees are written for a two-family residence.
Is the $85.00 a reinspection fee (Ordinance 2026-11) or an each-additional-unit fee (September 2026 form)? The FEE CHANGES 2025 web page still shows $175.00 / $80.00.
What does the Borough CCO inspection cover, and how far before closing should it be requested?
Are the fire bureau's rush fees ($150.00 / $210.00 for less than 1 week) still charged after Ordinance 2026-08, which only sets the two-weeks-ahead sale fee?
